content.comment_body: Hello, how can I save my [project_file] to a .BIN file? I was able to open a .BIN file in [product_name] version [version_no] and edit it, but after making changes, I want to provide the end user with an SD card containing the updated software. I can't find an option to save to .BIN file using 'Save as'. Is there a way to do this?
I figured it out. Right-click on the [article_no] device and select export.
Could your installation be corrupted? The 'Save As' option works fine for me.
I encountered an error: 'Java.Lang.NullPointerException'. The program runs well in simulation. Any advice or suggestions?

You can't save a Network Diagram directly to BIN. Instead, right-click on the [article_no] device and export as [project_file]. Then open that file and use 'Save as' to create the [product_name]_U_P.BIN file. This method is working for me now.

Hi, compared to an individual project file, a network project includes programs from all [product_name] devices in the setup. If two devices are part of the project, which program should be executed? Saving to x.bin only works when in single program mode. Hope this clarifies things.
A new question published by [user_name] has been split to a separate thread regarding modifying ladder diagrams in binary files. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering confusion when trying to export or save project files as .BIN for [product_name] devices using [product_name] version [version_no]. Issues highlighted include lack of clear instructions within the software, misunderstandings about managing network versus single device projects, and occasional technical errors such as Java.Lang.NullPointerException. Users desire an easy and error-free process for preparing software updates for SD card distribution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an intuitive and reliable process for exporting logic to .BIN files from [product_name] version [version_no], with comprehensive guidance and support for preparing files for SD card transfer, without encountering errors.
